body:
Confirmed — reproduced on 2.1.233 (Linux).

I built a minimal plugin with a `hooks/hooks.json` declaring SessionStart + PreToolUse hooks, installed it from a local marketplace (both directly and as an auto-installed dependency of another plugin, matching your `auto: true` setup) — and the hooks fired fine. The trigger is the `PreSkill` entry: `PreSkill` isn't a supported hook event, and one unrecognized event name currently causes the **entire** hooks.json to be rejected, so all the valid hooks (SessionStart, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse) silently never fire. Skills/agents are unaffected, and no error is shown at session start — the failure is only visible in `--debug` logs and as "failed to load" in `claude plugin list`.

That's a bug on our side: an unrecognized event should be skipped (with a visible warning), not silently disable every hook in the file. It also breaks plugins written for newer Claude Code versions when run on older ones. We're tracking a fix.

Workaround: remove the `PreSkill` entry from the plugin's hooks.json (or ask the plugin author to) — the remaining hooks will then register and fire.
